key_insight: State Transport Routing (STR) improves short-horizon photovoltaic forecasts by blending a frozen model’s output with two state-based trajectories from the latest measured power and recent trend.
engineering_relevance: STR is a lightweight, plug-in adapter that boosts neural PV forecasting accuracy without retraining the base model or changing its longer-horizon predictions.
method: Use the frozen forecast as the base trajectory.
Add two complementary states: latest measured power and recent trend.
Apply a horizon-conditioned router over the first 120 min; leave later horizons unchanged.
evidence_signal: Across four public PV datasets, STR outperformed a parameter-matched residual adapter, and on PVDAQ it improved five neural forecasting backbones with paired 95% confidence intervals excluding zero.
watch_item: Benefits were not reliable for LightGBM, so STR’s gains may depend on the underlying forecasting architecture.
paper_title: State Transport Routing for Short-horizon Adaptation in Multi-horizon Photovoltaic Forecasting
